To calculate the quenching percentages for the singlet and triplet states, we use the Stern-Volmer equation for dynamic quenching:
$$ \frac{I_0}{I} = 1 + k_q \tau_0 [Q] $$

- $I_0$ and $I$ are the emission intensities in the absence and presence of the quencher, respectively.
- $k_q$ is the bimolecular quenching rate constant.
- $\tau_0$ is the lifetime of the excited state in the absence of the quencher.
- $[Q]$ is the concentration of the quencher (the reductant, Red).

The fraction of the excited state that is quenched (quenching percentage) is given by:
$$ \text{Quenching \%} = \left( 1 - \frac{I}{I_0} \right) \times 100\% = \left( 1 - \frac{1}{1 + k_q \tau_0 [Q]} \right) \times 100\% = \frac{k_q \tau_0 [Q]}{1 + k_q \tau_0 [Q]} \times 100\% $$

$\alpha$-Cyclodextrin is inherently chiral due to the D-configuration of its glucopyranose units. $$\text{Number of distinct arrangements} = \frac{6!}{6} = \frac{720}{6} = 120$$
